articles.title: Blue Jackets Voronkov Could Become Next Shoe to Drop
articles.summary: The Columbus Blue Jackets may be the next team to make a move, with Dmitri Voronkov getting the most attention. The post Blue Jackets Voronkov Could Become N...
articles.body:
The Columbus Blue Jackets could have another trade situation developing, and Dmitri Voronkov might be the next shoe to drop in the NHL trade market.

The 26-year-old winger has appeared on the NHL trade radar after being scratched multiple times, raising questions about where he fits into the organization's plans.

Chris Johnston ranked Voronkov third on his latest trade board, while Pierre LeBrun reported that teams had contacted Columbus about the winger. More importantly, general manager Don Waddell reportedly confirmed receiving calls about Voronkov, although he indicated that no offers had been made.

That doesn't mean a trade is imminent, but there is enough smoke here to suggest something could be developing. And if Columbus is willing to listen, Voronkov could become the next shoe to drop in the NHL trade market.

Are the Blue Jackets Moving Voronkov Because He No Longer Fits?

The interesting question is whether Columbus is considering moving Voronkov because he no longer fits its plans or whether the organization is simply trying to use his trade value to acquire a different type of player.

That's the entire crux of the matter. Voronkov is a 26-year-old winger with size, a physical presence, and NHL scoring experience. Those qualities should make him attractive to teams looking for a complementary piece in their top nine.

He isn't necessarily the top-six scoring winger that several clubs are searching for, but that's not where his value lies. Voronkov can bring a different dimension to a forward group, providing some size and physicality while contributing offensively. For a contending team looking to round out its lineup, that could be an appealing combination.

The Blue Jackets also have to consider what they want their roster to look like under Rick Bowness. If they believe another type of forward would better complement their system, moving Voronkov could make sense even if they aren't necessarily unhappy with his overall talent.

In other words, this doesn't have to be a case of Columbus giving up on a player. It could simply be about finding a better stylistic fit.

A Voronkov Trade Could Happen Faster Than Expected

There is also a possibility that this situation develops faster than some pundits might expect. The Blue Jackets are trying to turn things around quickly, and they cannot afford to let their season get away from them while waiting for every roster decision to fall into place.

If Waddell believes Voronkov can bring back a player who better fits what Bowness wants to accomplish, there is little reason to drag out the process. The organization needs to make decisions that help its current roster while keeping its longer-term plans in mind.

Of course, Columbus shouldn't simply move Voronkov for the sake of making a trade. The return would have to be comparable in value, but ideally involve a player who offers a different stylistic fit. That could mean targeting a more versatile forward or someone who better complements the team's existing offensive pieces.

There is no indication that a deal is close, and the fact that Waddell hasn't received an offer worth pursuing is worth keeping in mind. Still, the interest is there, and Voronkov's repeated healthy scratches suggest his situation deserves attention.

The Blue Jackets have an opportunity to turn a potentially uncomfortable roster situation into an upgrade elsewhere. If the right offer arrives, Voronkov could be one of the more interesting names to watch as the trade market develops.

articles.title: Angels rumors: Potential Zach Neto trade update will catch shortstop-needing teams’ attention
articles.summary: A new era beckons for the Los Angeles Angels. After 23 years, Arte Moreno finally decided to give up ownership of the franchise — selling it to Kroenke Sport...
articles.body:
A new era beckons for the Los Angeles Angels . After 23 years, Arte Moreno finally decided to give up ownership of the franchise — selling it to Kroenke Sports & Entertainment for a reported $4 billion figure. And while the expectation is that, under new management, the Angels will be turning it around, they've been so bad for so long that it's going to take some time to get this team back to playing winning baseball.

To that end, it looks like the Angels, according to this insider, should at least be exploring the trade market for one of their best position players in shortstop Zach Neto, who recorded 27 home runs and 77 runs batted in across 157 games in 2026.

"This is the time to gauge interest in Zach Neto and Reid Detmers," MLB Network's Jon Morosi said on Hot Stove. "The Angels, I believe, have two of the most appealing names out there. When you talk about Neto in particular, I love his skillset and the way that he could potentially fit with any number of teams."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Only 25 years of age, Neto has three years of team control remaining, so the Angels should be in no rush to trade him away. But for Morosi, the Angels are so deep into their rebuild that it might be better off to cash in on Neto as a trade asset to replenish their farm system even further.

"The Angels are very much in a rebuilding phase. If you're looking at the Angels, this is a building job. It's not about winning a World Series in 2027. It's about building a consistent winner by the end of this decade. And if you're not gonna sign him long-term, think about ways to trade him now to get prospects," Morosi added.

Neto is averaging over 21 home runs per season in his career, and he's playing a premium defensive position, so the likely outcome here is that he starts the 2027 season with the Angels. But crazier things have happened in the trade market before.

articles.title: Klein Collins makes playoffs for 13th year in a row with convincing win over Klein Oak
articles.summary: Klein Collins broke a three-game losing streak to earn a spot in the Texas Class 6A Division I bi-district playoffs against Cypress Lakes.
articles.body:
Klein Collins hasn't missed out on the Texas high school football playoffs since 2013.

And the Tigers aren't going to start now.

Klein Collins secured its 13th consecutive postseason appearance with a 56-28 victory against Klein Oak on Thursday night at Klein Memorial Stadium in a game with straightforward win-or-go-home stakes.

The Tigers (6-4, 5-3) had lost three straight entering the final week of the regular season, including an ugly 50-point loss against district champion Klein last week. But they responded with their season on the line and were nearly unstoppable with their offensive run game against a Klein Oak team that had rattled off four consecutive wins. Klein Collins rushed for a season-high 407 yards and averaged a shade over 9 yards per attempt.

"Our kids were able to rise to the occasion, but not just tonight," said Klein Collins coach Adrian Mitchell, who took over the program in 2018. "They rose to the occasion Saturday by showing back up after arguably the worst Klein Collins football game in the history of the school. But they showed back up Saturday morning, right? And that's big. They showed up every day this week in practice, and then they showed up tonight."

Following last week's District 15-6A games, Klein, Tomball and Magnolia had already wrapped up three of the four playoff spots. That left the finale between Klein Collins and Klein Oak as a winner-take-all showdown. The Tigers made the most of the opportunity and will now get a chance to play another week. Klein Collins will take on Cypress Lakes (7-2, 5-1 in District 16-6A) in the bi-district round of the Class 6A Division I playoffs. The Spartans have won five consecutive games entering Friday's regular-season finale against Jersey Village and will be making their second consecutive playoff appearance.

"This is amazing," said senior quarterback Brylon Jefferson, who rushed for 134 yards and two touchdowns on 12 carries, including a 60-yarder on the first play from scrimmage. "Maybe three weeks ago, we might not have thought we were going to keep playing, but now we're here. So we're ready. We're coming, and we're ready."

Klein Oak (5-5, 5-3) was without the services of four-star junior running back Micah Rhodes, a Texas commit who had rushed for 1,043 yards. But the Panthers' struggles on defense were the primary culprit to their downfall. They entered the night second in the district at 236.5 yards allowed per game, but by the time the dust settled on the first half, Klein Collins had already racked up 303 rushing yards and 398 total en route to a commanding 42-20 lead.

Explosive plays were detrimental to Klein Oak's defensive efforts. Klein Collins had six rushing plays of 20-plus yards in the first half as Jefferson, Kobe Harmon and Da'Marcus Jones led the charge. Tyce Hudson also surpassed 1,000 all-purpose yards for the season with 95 receiving yards and a touchdown on two catches. Klein Oak finished with 228 yards in the first half and moved the ball well offensively, but the Panthers were unable to keep pace.

"If the O-line is the reason we got the first 15 yards, the receivers are the reason we get the 50-yard burst, the big, long touchdowns," said Mitchell, proudly showing off the white "DAWGS" lettering across the front of his navy blue shirt, meant to pay homage to the Klein Collins offensive line. "When those guys are blocking downfield, we're making it our mission for the DBs or whoever we're blocking to be so fighting mad by the end of the game that they want to throw a punch and they're going to get kicked out. We want to have that type of relentless effort throughout the game, and that's the mindset, and that's the mantra that our guys took into that game."

After surrendering 736 yards against Klein last week - including 536 passing with eight touchdowns from quarterback Carter Lattelle - the Klein Collins defense was motivated to make amends. The Tigers gave up some big plays in the first half, but the unit was lights-out following the intermission as the team extended its lead. Klein Collins surrendered just 15 yards in the third quarter and kept the Panthers off the scoreboard completely. Jayden Guillory had two interceptions in key situations for the Tigers, bringing his team-high season total to four.

On the offensive side, Harmon finished with 112 rushing yards and a touchdown on 12 carries, and Da'Marcus Jones rattled off a team-high 136 yards with three touchdowns on just nine attempts. Jones' 31-yard touchdown run with 8:24 remaining in the game was the cherry on top for what was a dominant night on the ground.

After three consecutive losses, the Tigers found themselves in a dire situation. But Mitchell said his team never lost belief in their quest for the postseason, and Jefferson echoed those sentiments. Now, after Klein Collins' most critical win of the season, he and his teammates will get a chance to see where the next matchup takes them.

"The season has been a roller coaster," Jefferson said. But I think we're coached well enough to persevere and get through whatever we need to get through to get to the next game."

articles.title: Hot and Cold Takes for Notre Dame VS Miami
articles.summary: The HOTTEST and COLDEST takes for Notre Dame VS Miami
articles.body:
This week has been wild. I have been on redeye flights going around the country while trying to keep up with the latest injuries news, line movements, and hot takes. This is the one we've all been waiting for….so let's let this rip.

Darian Mensah struggles early, but keeps Miami in the game with big plays before the half and late in the second half

Mensah has been fantastic…there is no sugarcoating it. He lost arguably the best weapon in college football with Malachi Toney being out, but that doesn't take away from just how good he has been. HOWEEEVAAA…this is, by far, the biggest moment and game of his career. He has faced ranked teams before, but those opponents were Virginia, Illinois, and Georgia Tech. They haven't faced a ranked team this year and have squeaked by against both UNC and FSU. Has Mensah been the reason for those struggles? Absolutely not. But he is heading into a buzzsaw of an environment without his top wideout and with a floundering defense. That's a lot of pressure to put on one guy!

I think the pressure and moment gets to him early. He'll come out slow, and the crowd will be all over him. I do expect him to settle in and respond, putting together a scoring drive late in the first half to either tie the game or bring it back to within one score. Finally, just as the Irish are ready to put Miami away, Mensah will also keep them in it with a late score with his legs…Mensah will struggle early, but finish with a solid showing despite losing his most potent weapon.

Carr has been very good this year. He's completing nearly 70% of his passes, has thrown 18 touchdowns, and has just one interception…and yet…there is still more to be desired. Carr has been a very good quarterback for Notre Dame, but he hasn't had a true "defining moment." In every big game, he has been somewhere between average and solid, operating more like a game manager than a difference-maker. That changes this week. CJ finally steps up and delivers an elite performance.

This is not the 2025 Miami defense, and this unit has shown some significant vulnerabilities over the last few weeks. Look for Notre Dame to dial up a double move early after Carr establishes his rhythm with the usual Faison completions. CJ will go for over 300 yards and three touchdowns through the air while adding a fourth on the ground, cementing a marquee moment for the beloved Irish QB.

articles.title: Postgame Reaction: The Avalanche’s Process Is Being Put to the Test
articles.summary: It’s been a while since the Avalanche have had to grind for 60 minutes in a close game. They only […]
articles.body:
It's been a while since the Avalanche have had to grind for 60 minutes in a close game. They only secured one point on Thursday night against the

It's been a while since the Colorado Avalanche have had to grind through 60 minutes of a close hockey game. They did plenty of things well Thursday night against the Nashville Predators, but couldn't find a way to get it across the finish line. The result was a 3-2 overtime loss and just one point to show for it.

In some ways, it was a different kind of night for Colorado. Most of its recent games have been decided by three or more goals, with the winning team usually pulling away. Thursday was a much tighter contest, one that required the Avalanche to find a way to win some of the smaller battles.

But in another sense, it was a familiar story. The power play couldn't deliver a go-ahead goal when it had the opportunity, and the opposition's man advantage ultimately provided the game-winner.

Colorado had a power play with 3:08 remaining in regulation and the score tied 2-2. It had opportunities to take the lead but couldn't convert. Then, in overtime, Steven Stamkos buried a four-on-three power-play goal to give Nashville the extra point.

It's a process for the Avs right now. They've struggled over the past couple of weeks and are facing adversity much earlier in the season than they did a year ago. There's something to be said for having to grind through a stretch like this, build some calluses and figure out how to get yourself out of it.

Head coach Jared Bednar seemed to appreciate the effort, even if the result wasn't what his team wanted.

"I think there's enough that we can show, and some things that we can continue to improve on," Bednar said, as the Avs fell to 6-1-2 at home. "I think they should feel good about their effort, you know, our effort, and that's where it starts for me. Now go repeat that same effort, clean some things up. Like this is a process. We're in game whatever it is, 17."

The standings aren't exactly screaming for concern, either. Colorado is 9-6-2 and currently eighth in the Western Conference. Had it secured the second point Thursday, it would have jumped to second in the Central Division.

Still, the Avalanche know there's work to do. And having to play through games like this could be beneficial as the season progresses.

"It's kind of like playoff hockey in a way. Everybody's defending well, low scoring, and just you know, kind of a gritty game," defenseman Sam Malinski said. "So yeah, it's good to play those right now."

Jaden Schwartz and Parker Kelly scored for Colorado, which is now 0-1-1 over its last two games after winning three straight. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 22 of 25 shots and fell to 8-3-1 on the season.

The message from the Avalanche after the game was to take the positives, learn from the negatives and move on.

"It's a stepping stone to where we want to go," defenseman Devon Toews said. "I think it's a better blueprint of what we need to do night in, night out, in order to have success in this league."

Toews hit the post in overtime before taking the penalty that led to Stamkos' game-winner.

The opening goal came from none other than Ross Colton. Nashville's forward buried the fourth shot of a flurry of opportunities around Blackwood's crease, putting the Predators ahead 4:01 into the game.

Nashville had the jump early and looked like the hungrier team throughout much of the first period. But the lead didn't last.

A strong forecheck from Brock Nelson helped the Avalanche get back into the game. Nelson chased the puck carrier behind the Nashville net and stripped him of possession. The puck eventually found Martin Necas, who set up Schwartz in the slot for his seventh goal of the season at 9:11.

That was Colorado's only goal of the opening period. Nashville eventually regained the lead with one of the more impressive first NHL goals you'll see.

Vitali Pinchuk, the undrafted 24-year-old rookie who joined the Predators as a free agent from the KHL, had very little room to work with. But he managed to get a backhand shot past Blackwood and into the top of the net. It was an incredibly difficult finish, and one that would be tough to replicate even if he tried.

The 2-1 Nashville lead lasted until 5:08 of the second period, when Kelly scored his third goal of the season.

The fourth-line winger found himself on a two-on-one with Fedor Svechkov. Kelly looked over at his linemate before deciding to keep the puck and shoot. It was the right decision. His release beat former Avalanche goaltender Justus Annunen over the shoulder and into the top of the net to tie the game at two.

Neither team found another goal in regulation.

Colorado finished 0-for-3 on the power play and 4-for-5 on the penalty kill. The Avalanche had successfully killed off four Nashville power plays before Toews' penalty in overtime gave the Predators the opening they needed.

The first period was sloppy. Bednar knew it, and the players knew it.

But after the first intermission, Colorado looked much more composed defensively. The Avalanche tightened things up, limited Nashville's opportunities and looked a lot more like the team that made defending a strength last season.

That's an important positive to take from this game. Defensive breakdowns have been an issue for Colorado during stretches of the past couple of weeks, but the team did a much better job of cleaning things up after the first period.

It wasn't perfect, but there was noticeable improvement as the game went along. Those are things you can build on.

This one ultimately came down to special teams.

Nashville entered Thursday with the fourth-best power play in the NHL, so the Avalanche knew they were going to have their hands full. Colorado's penalty kill did a good job for most of the night, shutting down four opportunities before the overtime sequence.

The Avalanche had a chance to take control of the game with just over three minutes remaining in regulation. Instead, they went without a goal on their third man advantage of the night. They generated some opportunities, but couldn't find the finish.

And then, when the Predators got their opportunity in overtime, they made Colorado pay.

articles.title: Teenage karting champion following track of Formula 1 heroes
articles.summary: A County Tyrone teenager is representing Ireland in a competition known as the Superbowl of karting.
articles.body:
A low hum becomes louder as an engine starts to rev.

The smell off of burning tyres is in the air and crowds start to gather.

It's not the practice grid of this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix, but a school car park where a teenager has his sights firmly on becoming the next karting champion to make it to Formula 1.

As the lunchtime bell rang, most pupils made their way to the canteen.

Thirteen-year-old Charlie Condy strode out of school, racing helmet in hand, towards his trusty go-kart, under the watchful eye of one of his teachers and his father, who is also his lead mechanic.

The Ballygawley teenager has been squeezing in last-minute practice sessions at Aughnacloy College in County Tyrone wherever possible as he prepares for the most important race of his life.

The Rotax World Grand Finals begin this weekend in Portugal and bring together the top go kart racers from across the globe.

After a hugely successful year winning countless domestic competitions, Charlie has been chosen to represent Team Ireland in the Junior event of the grand finals that are often referred to as the Superbowl of karting.

It has previously been won by some of the biggest names in motor sport and has been a launching pad to the prestigious and highly competitive world of Formula 1.

Even though he's still only 13, Charlie says he has been preparing for this race for most of his life.

He said: "My mum use to take me on her knee on our sit on lawnmower when I was about three and she said I was always trying to grab and take control of the steering wheel, so I've always been obsessed with driving.

"I got into karting at the age of five and I've just loved it ever since, there's nothing like the adrenaline and the sheer excitement of racing other people."

Charlie's success has been a team and family effort, with his mother and father taking on the roles of coach and mechanic.

His father, Ivor Condy, said he's extremely proud of Charlie, but watching the races can be nerve racking.

"The first lap or two are the worst when all the karts are bunched together, but once he gets going and they're spaced out, it settles you a little, and then I just hope I've done my part and the kart stays together and nothing falls off."

The Rotax MAX Challenge Grand Finals are an annual global championship. All drivers use similar engines, with a focus on driver skill rather than mechanical advantages.

Competitive go karting, also known as karting, is widely considered as one of the most direct environments in which young drivers can take to make it into elite motor sport.

Karting has been the training ground for many Formula 1 drivers.

Before becoming a household name in Formula 1, The four-time world champion, Max Verstappen, dominated the world of karting early in his career.

In September this year the Dutchman went back to his roots and took part in an exhibition go-kart race at Silverstone.

Closer to home, hugely successful Belfast-born racing driver Charlie Eastwood also began his career in competitive karting.

In 2012 he became Ireland's first Karting World Champion.

At the age of 17 he won the Rotax Max World Championship – the same competition that young Charlie Condy will compete in this weekend.

Since then Eastwood's career has gone from strength to strength.

In 2020 he won the prestigious Le Mans 24-hour race and would go onto work with the Mercedes F1 team as a simulator driver.

These days he competes in the World Endurance Championship and is a factory driver for Corvette.

Eastwood said karting is the best start for any young person who has serious ambitions about competitive motor sport.

"It's such a great platform for young drivers to show what they can do, and for me being 17 and winning the Rotax Max World championship, it is still one of my most special wins, as a lot took off from there," he said.

"A lot of the F1 grade drivers today got their start in karting

"I remember having a number of pretty hard battles with Max Verstappen on the karting track, and in the last 10 years or so the competitions have been getting such a huge profile."

Eastwood said he'd been keeping a close eye on Charlie Condy's career.

"He'll be competing against the top two or three drivers in his age range from basically every corner of the globe, so to get access to that level of competition at the age of 13 is a huge opportunity."

Charlie has recently been nominated as the Mid Ulster Young Sports Person of the Year and locally some are referring to him as County Tyrone's answer to Lewis Hamilton.

But the Ballygawley teenager is taking it all in his stride and says his focus for now is firmly on the Rotax World Grand Finals.

He added: "Anything can happen in this sport, I'm just thinking about the races ahead and want to make sure I'm up at the front, that's the main thing."

articles.title: Divine Mukasa is doing exactly what Manchester City will have hoped to see at West Ham
articles.summary: Manchester City had a goal in mind when they sent Divine Mukasa out on loan to West Ham for the 2026-27 season. Rather than spend the season on the periphery...
articles.body:
Manchester City had a goal in mind when they sent Divine Mukasa out on loan to West Ham for the 2026-27 season. Rather than spend the season on the periphery of Enzo Maresca's squad, it was hoped that Mukasa could develop as a player by playing regularly for the Hammers. That is exactly what has transpired in the 14 games that Mukasa has played so far this season. The gifted young midfielder continues to grow as a player and the more he impresses at West Ham the more you think that Mukasa could one day be destined for a role at Manchester City.

Divine Mukasa continues to impress for West Ham as he is now an important player for the Hammers.

West Ham haven't hit the ground running in the Championship this season. They sit eighth on the table and that form saw Nuno Espirito Santo sacked as their manager. Scott Parker is now the West Ham manager. Under Nuno, Divine Mukasa played in a deeper midfield role. Playing in a new role allowed Mukasa to show another side to his game. He was able to dictate the tempo of matches and show that he is up to the challenge of playing in midfield in the Championship.

West Ham sacked Nuno Espirito Santo after their 3-1 defeat to West Brom at the beginning of November. Scott Parker replaced Nuno and took charge of West Ham's 3-3 draw with Cardiff City . Cardiff City took a 3-0 lead in the 39th minute of that match. West Ham fought back to claim a point as they finished 3-3.

It was Divine Mukasa who scored West Ham's first goal against Cardiff City in the 58th minute. Parker utilized Mukasa as an attacking midfielder in the match. The Manchester City youngster made a smart run through the heart of the Cardiff City defence. Jarrod Bowen picked out Mukasa's run with a great ball over the top. Mukasa then produced a sublime chip to beat Cardiff City keeper Yousef Salech, setting the stage for West Ham's comeback. That goal illustrated what Mukasa can do playing in arguably his best position.

Manchester City will be thrilled to see Divine Mukasa's progress and growth as a player.

Divine Mukasa has shown his versatility and talent in the fourteen matches he has played for West Ham this season. Yes, at times Mukasa is inconsistent and on occasions drifts out of games. That is to be expected from a 19-year-old playing in an underperforming side. There is an argument to be made that Nuno Espirito Santo played Mukasa out of position. However, playing in a deeper midfield role did allow Mukasa to show another side to his game aside from his creativity and eye for goals. Scott Parker may decide to unleash Mukasa as an attacking midfielder. His performance against Cardiff suggests that the Manchester City loanee will remain a key component of Scott Parker's lineup.

From a Manchester City point of view, they will be thrilled with the progress that Divine Mukasa is making as a player. When he was loaned out to West Ham, the hope was that Mukasa would establish himself in the Hammers starting lineup and develop as a player. The early indications are that this is what is occurring. Manchester City will be thrilled with this as Divine Mukasa does figure to be an important player in the future for Manchester City.

articles.title: Ahmad Hardy injury timeline: How Mizzou RB made incredible return to football after shooting
articles.summary: Ahmad Hardy is back in Missouri colors after being injured in a shooting six months ago. Here's how he did it.
articles.body:
Missouri ascent up the SEC standings has been spurred on by its run game. The Tigers are at their best when they're gashing teams in the trenches.

Ahmad Hardy was at the heart of Missouri's ground-based attack last year, producing a conference-best 1,649 yards in his maiden season en route to landing consensus All-American honors. He figured to play a similar role in the Tigers' offense this season before being cutdown by a gunshot wound to the leg.

Just six months after falling victim to a stray bullet, however, Hardy is already ahead of schedule. The 5-10, 210-pound running back returned to the field in style in the Tigers' last game. He could stand to see more time as the season wears on, especially if Missouri is able to stay close to the CFP race.

With that, here's a look at how Hardy recovered from his devastating injuries to add another dimension to the Tigers' high-octane attack.

Hardy was struck by a bullet while leaving a concert in Laurel, Mississippi early on May 10. He was an innocent bystander in the shooting, described as a "melee" by attending police officers

Hardy was shot in the upper leg, with the bullet striking a bone. He underwent surgery shortly after the shooting, returning to the team's facility in Columbia to rehab.

Three individuals were arrested in connection with the shooting. One was eventually charged with two felony counts of aggravated assault.

Hardy took to Missouri's practice facility shortly after undergoing surgery, using the grounds as a place to regain his lower-body strength. All signs pointed to Hardy returning to the field, although it was unclear when that would be the case.

Head coach Eli Drinkwitz offered few updates on Hardy's status in the lead-up to the campaign, ostensibly attempting to divert pressure away from his star tailback. The extent of damage Hardy suffered to his leg is still unknown, although Drinkwitz indicated that the 20-year-old running back needed to have a metal rod inserted in his femur.

Hardy credited his teammates and faith with helping uplift him during his recovery.

"Me, mentally, I'm a very strong mental person," Hardy said, per the Associated Press. "Whatever I put my mind to, I can do it. If the good Lord said I can do it, then I can do it."

He made his long-awaited return to action on Halloween, making two carries for five yards in the Tigers' 34-10 win over Arkansas. Drinkwitz made mention of him in his postgame presser, praising the senior in his opening statement.

"I want to say I'm really, really proud of Ahmad Hardy," Drinkwitz said. "It's been a long road to get back here. It's been a very difficult challenge for everybody. ... To be able to come in here and get us a big first down, I'm really proud of him."

articles.title: Klopp leaves out Adeyemi: Weidenfeller has a theory
articles.summary: No place in Germany’s squad: Weidenfeller suspects defensive weaknesses are behind Adeyemi’s omission. Karim Adeyemi’s exclusion from the squad for the upcom...
articles.body:
No place in Germany's squad: Weidenfeller suspects defensive weaknesses are behind Adeyemi's omission. Karim Adeyemi's exclusion from the squad for the upcoming internationals against Serbia and the Netherlands has sparked debate.

Former Germany goalkeeper Roman Weidenfeller offered his theory on why the attacking player is missing from national team coach Jürgen Klopp's squad on Sky's "Triple – Der Hagedorn-Fußballtalk."

According to Weidenfeller, the main reason is a lack of defensive work. Although Adeyemi had performed reasonably well in attack—notably against the Netherlands, even though he missed a potential winner—Weidenfeller spotted weaknesses in his tracking back during the match against Greece.

Under Klopp, players enjoy plenty of freedom going forward, but tracking back is mandatory. Since Adeyemi had sometimes been too hesitant in that regard, Weidenfeller suggested his omission could be a deliberate warning from the national team coach.

TV pundit Dietmar Hamann also expressed surprise at the decision, stressing that players with Adeyemi's tremendous pace are few and far between in the squad. Beyond the tactical details, Adeyemi's current club situation may also have played a part: following inconsistent performances for his club, other attacking players moved ahead of him in the pecking order this time.

articles.title: Hillsdale shakes off slow start to down Lake Center in regionals
articles.summary: After shaking off regional jitters in the first set, the Falcons looked every bit the team that now has 20 wins this season.
articles.body:
UNIONTOWN - Jillian Cowger had never experienced anything like Thursday's match against Lake Center Christian.

Not just because it was Hillsdale's first regional appearance in volleyball since 1976, but Lake High School's gymnasium holds approximately 2,000 people and it was jam-packed for a Division VI regional semifinal between the Falcons and Tigers.

"I couldn't even hear anything my teammates were saying unless we were huddled in the middle," Cowger said. "It was pretty insane ... but that fuels me personally, hearing all the loud energy.

"I love a loud crowd and that was great."

It was great indeed for the Falcons who shook off a sluggish opening set to take the next three for a 19-25, 25-22, 25-21, 25-20 win to advance to the regional championship for the first time in — you guessed it — 50 years.

"I'm honestly speechless," Cowger said. "It's a very surreal feeling because all the work we've put in is paying off. Over the past four years, it's finally paying off."

Hillsdale went down 4-0 in the first set and then 7-1 forcing coach Matti Willeke into using her first timeout. The Falcons kept the game within reach, but couldn't overcome the slow start despite matching the Tigers at 18-18 over the remainder of the set after the timeout.

"We've never played in a gym with that amount of noise where you can barely hear the person because you," Willeke said. "We were just vibrating at a really high level, we needed to calm our nervous system back down to get settled in.

"(And) we did settle into the (first) game, so it was more so let's just continue that. We're good, we found our rhythm at the end of the game, we just found it too late — let's keep it going."

Once they settled into unfamiliar territory, the Falcons looked a lot more like the team that won 20 games.

"It's definitely a different atmosphere than we're used to — a lot louder — so we had to acclimate to that," Cowger said. "But once we got used to it and got the jitters out, we started settling in and started to play our game better."

Hillsdale stormed out to an 11-6 lead in the second set and stretched it to 18-13 before getting set-point at 24-18. Lake Center tried to rally winning four consecutive points before the Falcons closed out to even the match.

And it was a similar story in the third and fourth sets as Hillsdale stretched a lead, saw it nearly slip away, but managed to close out for just the program's second regional semifinal win.

"Like any volleyball match, you know how quickly it can turn to the other side," Lake Center Christian coach Hannah Miller said. "It's tiring coming out that hard then trying to keep that up, but the girls did well fighting back. And throughout this season in tough matches, win or lose, they've fought and they keep fighting."

While the Falcons struggled with the atmopshere early, the Tigers embraced it as they have all season long.

"We made history coming to regionals," Miller said. "Lake Center had never been here, and last year we made it to the district final for the first time. It was a totally different environment ... very hyped, a lot of love from our fans and supporters. They all came out and it was amazing to feel the love from them this year."

In each of Hillsdale's sets won, a different senior hitter stepped up to ensure the result was a positive one. Cowger was instrumental in closing out the second set, Jordyn Fickes wowed in the third set, and Kiki McFadden was unstoppable in the fourth.

"I know when I come into games, my job is to change the tempo, make the ball better for my teammates, and try as hard as we can," Cowger said finishing with 14 kills, four solo blocks, and two aces.

Fickes had a season-high 16 kills with two aces, McFadden led all with 19 kills, 18 digs, and two aces. Sophomore Emily Smith had a career-best 47 assists in a four-set match — she matched or topped it three times earlier but in five sets — along with two aces, and senior Gracie Bishop had 15 digs.

"Once we got our server in place and putting balls up to Kiki and Jill, they really took care of the ball," Willeke said. "They were composed under pressure, even when they got blocked a couple times, they continued to put the ball in play."

Hillsdale now shifts its focus to Saturday's regional championship at Barberton High School. The Falcons get a third shot at Wayne County Athletic League rival Dalton who won earlier in the night in straight sets 25-22, 25-14, 25-8 over Independence.

"It's surreal," Willeke said. "It's just exiting to continue to win and now Dalton is a little familiar to us. Even though it's regional finals, that familiarity makes it more like — OK, let's go get Dalton. It's fun to be challenged by a team we already know."

Having lost both regular season meetings with the Bulldogs, Hillsdale has a chance to avenge those and make a half-century long return to state.

"They're so solid," Willeke said. "It's really about our composure ... we know every team is going to mess up and make their own errors, it's if we can make less unforced errors and put balls in play, take care of our serves and serve revive. We'll win games if we can take care of that first touch ... they're not easily rattled, so we just gotta keep our composure."

"We definitely need to work on finishing games, keeping our composure, and not letting the other side's momentum get to us," Cowger added. "We gotta work on keeping our side steady and get a good first pass, first serve ... basically just play our game without letting the moment get too big for us."

articles.title: Warned coach selected by English Gymnastics for international junior competition
articles.summary: A coach who received a formal warning from British Gymnastics following an investigation is coaching at an international youth competition this weekend.
articles.body:
A gymnastics coach who received a formal warning from British Gymnastics following an investigation into allegations including fear-based coaching and controlling practices is coaching at an international youth competition this weekend, BBC Sport has learned.

Clare Hague, head coach at Dronfield Gymnastics Academy near Sheffield, has travelled with English Gymnastics to coach at the Horizon Cup in Greece.

Complainants from two separate investigations into Hague and her club have told the BBC the decision is a "smack in the teeth" and "adds salt in the wound" for those who have had the courage to speak up about their concerns.

Documents seen by the BBC list fear-based coaching and emotional harm, controlling and restrictive practices, punitive attendance policies and psychological impact on children as some of the concerns considered in a recently concluded investigation.

The outcome letter, also seen by BBC Sport, states that British Gymnastics upheld a number of the concerns raised, issuing Hague and Dronfield Gymnastics Academy with a formal warning lasting two years - alongside monitoring and development measures.

The governing body did not share with the complainants which specific concerns had been upheld.

While Hague did not respond directly to a request for comment, Dronfield Gymnastics Academy shared a statement with the BBC stating the club co-operated "openly, fully and with complete transparency" with the investigation.

"We are pleased the investigation found no serious issue for Dronfield to address and that British Gymnastics received positive reports from members about their experience at the club. Following the concerns raised, the club has worked proactively and positively alongside British Gymnastics to see where improvements can be made so that a positive experience is the case for everyone," it said.

Hague, who is also squad co-ordinator for Yorkshire Women's Artistic Gymnastics, was announced by English Gymnastics as a coach for the Horizon Cup while she was still under investigation.

The Horizon Cup is an international artistic gymnastics competition for junior and pre-junior gymnasts aged 11-16.

English Gymnastics is an affiliated home country association under British Gymnastics and manages some regional and national programmes, including selection for Team England at the Commonwealth Games.

One complainant, speaking anonymously for fear of the repercussions for her daughter in the local gymnastics community, alleged to the BBC that they had raised concerns some gymnasts at Dronfield Gymnastics Academy regularly felt afraid to ask to go to the toilet - resulting in some wetting themselves and others choosing not to drink during sessions.

Allowing gymnasts opportunities to drink water throughout training and to go to the toilet at the earliest available opportunity was one of a number of safeguarding rules introduced by British Gymnastics in 2023 to stop practices it said were "on the fringes of abuse".

"We tell our kids to tell a trusted adult when something's wrong," the complainant told the BBC.

"My daughter had the courage to say something to try and protect the next child. I don't want the lesson she walks away with from this to be that there's no point in speaking up because nothing happens."

A complainant in another investigation into Hague, in 2022, alleged to the BBC their daughter endured years of emotional and physical abuse at Dronfield Gymnastics Academy. The outcome letter of that investigation, also seen by the BBC, said the coaches would be offered further training.

"I didn't have faith in the system in 2022 because it was notorious that the system was not working… I did have hope that things had changed but it's disappointing to know that the outcome effectively is the same," the complainant said.

That investigation concluded just months after an independent report - the Whyte Review - described systemic physical and emotional abuse within gymnastics in Britain and found wellbeing and welfare had "not been at the centre of British Gymnastics' culture".

The review made 17 recommendations focused on safeguarding and welfare, complaints handling, standards and educations, and governance and oversight, prompting the governing body to double its spending on welfare and safe sport to about £1m a year.

In a statement, British Gymnastics told BBC Sport they cannot comment on the specifics of individual cases but said every concern is treated "in a way appropriate to the nature of the case".

"We have a duty to all those involved to ensure that outcomes are based on a fair, balanced and thorough assessment of all information from any relevant people, with a full context and understanding of the situation and consideration of all perspectives," it said in a statement.

"We can be categoric that if we considered a member to be a risk they would be removed from our sport.

"With regards to Dronfield, it's important to highlight we have heard positive reports from members about their experience there. From any concerns raised, the club is proactively and positively working with us to see where improvements can be made so that positive experience is the case for everyone."

But campaigners argue cases such as this raise "alarming" questions about how concerns are identified, monitored and addressed, and challenge the efficacy of offering retraining for coaches who have had complaints against them upheld on more than one occasion.

"Where there are multiple complaints over multiple years, we cannot understand how it's possible that coaches are repeatedly being given retraining instead of adequate sanctions to get them out of the sport, because they're proving consistently they are inappropriate coaches to be working with children," Claire Heafford, chief executive of campaign group Gymnasts for Change, told BBC Sport.

British Gymnastics began publishing the names of banned and expelled coaches in 2023 as part of its 'Reform 25' programme, but Heafford claims this is "meaningless" as it does not extend to those who have had sanctions against them.

"If you're the parent of an athlete at the moment, you have no way of knowing whether the coach coaching your child has had previous complaints or sanctions against them," she said.

"That is an awful situation for parents and athletes to be in and in this case, it proves that the current system is continuing to put children in harm's way."

articles.title: Lakers' defense was good in win over Kings, says coach JJ Redick
articles.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick saw some growth in his team's defense during its win over the Kings on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Defense was a sizable concern for the Los Angeles Lakers coming into this season, especially considering they were 20th in defensive rating last season, and it remains a concern. Through nine games, they rank 21st in defensive rating, 25th in opponents' points off turnovers per game and last in opponents' second-chance points per game.

In Wednesday's game against the Sacramento Kings , the Lakers fell behind early due to their defense. With 5:36 left in the first quarter, they were down 18-11 and looked to be in some trouble. But at that point, they pulled themselves together and ended the period tied at 28, and they powered their way to a 116-103 victory .

It wasn't exactly a good offensive outing for Los Angeles, but for a change, its defense allowed it to come away with a win. Coach JJ Redick outlined how their defense came through during this contest in Northern California, via Lakers Nation .

"Any time you can get a stop, it's great," Redick said on Spectrum SportsNet after the win. "Ideally, you can get a stop without the other team shooting the ball. I think when the game started, we were a little flat. I called an early timeout when they had 16 points, they scored 87 for the last 43 minutes and 27 seconds or whatever it was after I called that timeout. So the defense was good. Still, execution-wise, game plan-wise, Stan Van Gundy always used to say if 10 guys play and each guy has a 'my bad, I messed that one up. My bad.' That's 10 mistakes. That could be 20 points, that could be 30 points. "I think as we grow and we become hopefully a great basketball team, we're gonna limit those game plan errors, those my bads. The promising thing on that side of the ball is the effort and the intent to execute I think is really high. Second efforts were really good. We had a number of veer switches and peel switches and scrambles, had a number of late shot clock possessions and shot clock violations. We did a lot on that end and I think the activity overall was really good, save for the first four minutes or whatever it was."

L.A. held the Kings to 38.9% field-goal shooting and 31.6% from 3-point range, and it forced the Kings into 18 turnovers while coming up with 11 steals and 13 blocks. The Purple and Gold have been excelling at forcing mistakes -- they currently rank third in opponents' turnover percentage, as well as first in points off turnovers per game.

Of course, their offense has largely carried them to a 7-2 record. They're third in 3-point accuracy, second in points per game and first in field-goal percentage and offensive rating, and they're even sixth in fast-break points per game.

Luka Doncic is on a potentially special run to start the campaign, and he's putting up 38.5 points, 8.1 rebounds and eight assists a game while shooting 49.5% overall, 43.1% from 3-point range and 89.3% from the free throw line. He has scored at least 40 points in his last three games and five of his last six contests, and he's making it look very routine.
